graphEvents.label: One line per file plus reported elision design

label: The flood is live in the shipped wrapper: structured search for 'iteration' over this packet's research dir returned 190 ranked rows across 6 files, max 34 in one file, and the first 20 display rows all came from that single file.
The only cap today is presentation-only: search() returns every ranked match in record.results, formatSummary slices the first 20 for humans, and --json emits the full array through stableStringify.

structuredCappedRecipe has zero callers anywhere in the repository; its only code occurrence is the definition, the wrapper's structured builder is uncapped, and assertRecipeParity compares only the uncapped lane builder.

Wiring --max-count 1 into the fetch would keep each file's earliest matching line rather than its best-ranked line and would destroy the per-file counts the elision needs, so the capped builder's rationale is wrong on both counts.

Totals come free from the same rg run: the uncapped structured fetch already parses every match and rankMatches returns every row, so per-file counts are one Map pass with no count recipe and no second invocation.
The rank tuple sorts by evidence field, match class, path, line, so the first occurrence of a path is its best-ranked line and the guarantee pass is a filter over ordered rows, never a second ranker.

Compatibility surface: retrofit-convention.mjs is the only non-test caller of search() and reads resultCount from results.length; the ranking test puts trigger and body matches in one file and will fail under one-line-per-file; formatSummary and search-presentation.txt report a shown count with no hidden count.
The keyed lane already defines --limit, default 20, 0 lifts the cap, and validates a whole decimal, so the wrapper should reuse that vocabulary instead of adding --k.
Shaping filters the rank tuple's ordered rows and never re-sorts them, so the tuple remains the lane's only ranker and output stays deterministic.
Elision totals are exact only while the structured fetch stays uncapped; --max-count destroys the per-file counts the elision reports.
The answer must report every bound it applies: moreInFile per row and hidden files/matches plus matchCount, fileCount, limit and truncated on the record.
Live bounded measurement of the shipped wrapper: 190 rows, 6 files, max 34 per file, first 20 display rows from one file.
Repository-wide grep confirms structuredCappedRecipe is dead code with a single definition and no callers.
